Subject: Token floor offsets & heartbeat credit question

Jonas —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Procurement and engineering dug through our sample invoices and we have a couple of follow-ups before we route an approval. Two quick items: 

1) Token floor offsets: we see line-items where short bursts are being rounded up to the floor and showing a >2x effective unit overage for small, frequent calls. Is there a documented offset or smoothing rule that applies when a customer has a high prefix reuse rate? We want to make sure the math on our side matches how you aggregate.

2) Heartbeat credits / warm-starts: our embeddings pipeline opens many ephemeral sessions that rely on a warm KV cache. Are these heartbeat tokens eligible for a credit or separate seat-based allowance? If so, what is the process to request it and what evidence do you need from us?

I've attached a small sample (BrightCart_usage_sample.csv) showing three typical days. Procurement is expecting a short note we can attach to the SOW.

Appreciate a clear process so we can finalize the order.

Best,
Alicia Gomez

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Token floor offsets & heartbeat credit question

Alicia —

Thanks for the sample and for surfacing these concerns. Short answers up front: yes, we have smoothing behavior and a heartbeat credit workflow; details below and a suggested next step.

Token floor offsets:
- Rounding: we apply per-request unitization with a minimum quantum (typically 16 tokens for short-LLM calls on this plan). Rounding happens after session aggregation when calls map to the same conversation bucket within a rolling window.
- Offset logic: for customers with high prefix reuse (you called this out), we run an affinity-based subsumption step that groups calls by prefix hash and applies a per-prefix amortization before applying the floor. That usually reduces the apparent overage for high-reuse workloads.
- What we need: the CSV you sent is perfect; we also ask for a representative 24-hour sample across peak/off-peak so we can run a quick amortization sim.

Heartbeat credits / warm-starts:
- We do offer a heartbeat allowance pilot for customers with many ephemeral sessions. It isn't automatic — it's a commercial concession tied to commit level.
- Evidence: usage samples, a short architecture note showing ephemeral session counts, and a request on company letterhead are sufficient to start. Technical evidence should call out: average session TTL, KV cache miss rate at cold start, and % of calls that are purely prefix-only.
- Process: 1) you submit the evidence, 2) we run a one-week simulation on our side, 3) the team recommends a credit band (e.g., 5-15% of monthly token bill as heartbeat allowance) and we formalize it in the SOW.

Attached is a brief process doc (RC_heartbeat-credit-process.pdf) that maps the steps and the internal owners. If you'd like, we can run a draft simulation using the CSV you shared — happy to queue that once procurement gives the go-ahead.

Proposed next step: if procurement is OK, can procurement/procure@brightcart.com confirm a 24-hour peak sample and authorize Redwood to simulate? We can return a one-page note suitable for attachment to the SOW within 72 business hours.

Cheers,
Jonas Weber
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Attachment: RC_heartbeat-credit-process.pdf (pdf, 18KB)
